title: Different sub-application behaviour when using FastAPI(root_path=...) vs --root-path CLI option
body:
### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from starlette.routing import get_route_path root_app = FastAPI() sub_app = FastAPI() root_app.mount("/subapp", sub_app) @root_app.get("/test") async def root_test(path: str, request: Request): return { "app": "root", "root_path": request.scope.get("root_path", ""), "path": request.scope.get("path", ""), "route_path": get_route_path(request.scope), } @sub_app.get("/test") async def sub_test(path: str, request: Request): return { "app": "sub", "root_path": request.scope.get("root_path", ""), "path": request.scope.get("path", ""), "route_path": get_route_path(request.scope), } ``` ### Description I am creating a FastAPI application that is served behind a proxy which strips part of the path, so I've been following the [Proxy with a stripped path prefix](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/behind-a-proxy/#proxy-with-a-stripped-path-prefix) docs. I am also using mounted sub-applications to handle API versioning (e.g. mounted at `/v1` and `/v2` for separate docs). Initially, I was using the `root_path` parameter in the FastAPI constructor to configure the stripped-path prefix, which works as expected for the root application, but I experienced unexpected behaviour adding the sub-applications. --- `tl;dr` According to the [FastAPI docs](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/behind-a-proxy/#setting-the-root-path-in-the-fastapi-app): > Passing the `root_path` to `FastAPI` would be the equivalent of passing the `--root-path` command line option to Uvicorn or Hypercorn. However, my experience has shown that these configuration methods result in different behaviour for the request scope `path` which seems to break route matching in mounted sub-applications when using the `root_path` parameter. --- **With no root path configuration:**
```GET /test - 200 OK ✅``` ```GET /subapp/test - 200 OK ✅```
```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "", "path": "/test", "route_path": "/test", } ``` ```json json { "app": "sub", "root_path": "/subapp", "path": "/subapp/test", "route_path": "/test", } ```
**OpenAPI schema:** `/openapi.json` and `/subapp/openapi.json` With no root path configuration, the behaviour is as expected. --- **Root path configured via FastAPI CLI with `--root-path="/api"`:**
```GET /test - 200 OK ✅``` ```GET /subapp/test - 200 OK ✅```
```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "/api", "path": "/api/test", "route_path": "/test", } ``` ```json json { "app": "sub", "root_path": "/api/subapp", "path": "/api/subapp/test", "route_path": "/test", } ```
```GET /api/test - 404 Not Found ❌``` ```GET /api/subapp/test - 404 Not Found ❌```
```json json { "detail": "Not Found" } ``` ```json json { "detail": "Not Found" } ```
**OpenAPI schema:** `/api/openapi.json` and `/api/subapp/openapi.json` When configuring the root path via the FastAPI CLI option, the routes can be accessed at `localhost:8000/test` and `localhost:8000/subapp/test` as expected, since the `/api` root path would be stripped by the proxy. It is not possible to access the routes by including the root path in the requests when using the CLI option (as shown by the 404s). The OpenAPI schema is served with the root path prefixed so the Swagger UI can access it from outside the proxy (as described in the [FastAPI docs](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/behind-a-proxy/#check-the-docs-ui)) --- **Root path configured via FastAPI constructor with `root_path="/api"`:**
```GET /test - 200 OK ✅``` ```GET /subapp/test - 404 Not Found ❌```
```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "/api", "path": "/test", "route_path": "/test", } ``` ```json json { "detail": "Not Found" } ```
```GET /api/test - 200 OK ✅``` ```GET /api/subapp/test - 200 OK ✅```
```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "/api", "path": "/api/test", "route_path": "/test", } ``` ```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "/api/subapp", "path": "/api/subapp/test", "route_path": "/test", } ```
**OpenAPI schema:** `/api/openapi.json` and `/api/subapp/openapi.json` Note that `/docs` and `/api/docs` work (and both fetch the OpenAPI JSON schema correctly), but `/subapp/docs` doesn't work – only `/api/subapp/docs` works. When configuring the root path via the FastAPI `root_path` constructor parameter, the root FastAPI app route can be accessed at `localhost:8000/test` as expected, **BUT** the sub-application route can no longer be accessed without the root path in the URL. Additionally, the behaviour continues to deviate since now it is possible to access the root app route by including the root path in the request which was not possible with the CLI option. The OpenAPI schema is served with the root path prefixed so the Swagger UI can access it from outside the proxy, but now the UI does not show a "Failed to load API definition" Fetch error. ### Operating System macOS ### Operating System Details macOS Sequoia 15.1.1 (24B91) ### FastAPI Version 0.135.1 ### Pydantic Version 2.11.4 ### Python Version 3.12.9 ### Additional Context This behaviour is described in another [discussion post](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/11959) from 2024, but I wasn't sure if necroposting in the comments was appropriate. I thought I would make a new discussion and hopefully be able to resolve the old discussion along with this one.

Commit to Help

 I commit to help with one of those options 👆

Example Code
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from starlette.routing import get_route_path

root_app = FastAPI()
sub_app = FastAPI()

root_app.mount("/subapp", sub_app)

@root_app.get("/test")
async def root_test(path: str, request: Request):
    return {
        "app": "root",
        "root_path": request.scope.get("root_path", ""),
        "path": request.scope.get("path", ""),
        "route_path": get_route_path(request.scope),
    }

@sub_app.get("/test")
async def sub_test(path: str, request: Request):
    return {
        "app": "sub",
        "root_path": request.scope.get("root_path", ""),
        "path": request.scope.get("path", ""),
        "route_path": get_route_path(request.scope),
    }
Description
I am creating a FastAPI application that is served behind a proxy which strips part of the path, so I've been following the Proxy with a stripped path prefix docs. I am also using mounted sub-applications to handle API versioning (e.g. mounted at /v1 and /v2 for separate docs).
Initially, I was using the root_path parameter in the FastAPI constructor to configure the stripped-path prefix, which works as expected for the root application, but I experienced unexpected behaviour adding the sub-applications.

tl;dr According to the FastAPI docs:

Passing the root_path to FastAPI would be the equivalent of passing the --root-path command line option to Uvicorn or Hypercorn.

However, my experience has shown that these configuration methods result in different behaviour for the request scope path which seems to break route matching in mounted sub-applications when using the root_path parameter.

With no root path configuration:


 
GET /test - 200 OK ✅


GET /subapp/test - 200 OK ✅




json
{
    "app": "root",
    "root_path": "",
    "path": "/test",
    "route_path": "/test",
}


json
{
    "app": "sub",
    "root_path": "/subapp",
    "path": "/subapp/test",
    "route_path": "/test",
}



OpenAPI schema: /openapi.json and /subapp/openapi.json
With no root path configuration, the behaviour is as expected.

Root path configured via FastAPI CLI with --root-path="/api":


 
GET /test - 200 OK ✅


GET /subapp/test - 200 OK ✅




json
{
    "app": "root",
    "root_path": "/api",
    "path": "/api/test",
    "route_path": "/test",
}


json
{
    "app": "sub",
    "root_path": "/api/subapp",
    "path": "/api/subapp/test",
    "route_path": "/test",
}



 
GET /api/test - 404 Not Found ❌


GET /api/subapp/test - 404 Not Found ❌




json
{
    "detail": "Not Found"
}


json
{
    "detail": "Not Found"
}



OpenAPI schema: /api/openapi.json and /api/subapp/openapi.json
When configuring the root path via the FastAPI CLI option, the routes can be accessed at localhost:8000/test and localhost:8000/subapp/test as expected, since the /api root path would be stripped by the proxy.
It is not possible to access the routes by including the root path in the requests when using the CLI option (as shown by the 404s). The OpenAPI schema is served with the root path prefixed so the Swagger UI can access it from outside the proxy (as described in the FastAPI docs)

Root path configured via FastAPI constructor with root_path="/api":


 
GET /test - 200 OK ✅


GET /subapp/test - 404 Not Found ❌




json
{
    "app": "root",
    "root_path": "/api",
    "path": "/test",
    "route_path": "/test",
}


json
{
    "detail": "Not Found"
}



 
GET /api/test - 200 OK ✅


GET /api/subapp/test - 200 OK ✅




json
{
    "app": "root",
    "root_path": "/api",
    "path": "/api/test",
    "route_path": "/test",
}


json
{
    "app": "root",
    "root_path": "/api/subapp",
    "path": "/api/subapp/test",
    "route_path": "/test",
}



OpenAPI schema: /api/openapi.json and /api/subapp/openapi.json
Note that /docs and /api/docs work (and both fetch the OpenAPI JSON schema correctly), but /subapp/docs doesn't work – only /api/subapp/docs works.
When configuring the root path via the FastAPI root_path constructor parameter, the root FastAPI app route can be accessed at localhost:8000/test as expected, BUT the sub-application route can no longer be accessed without the root path in the URL.
Additionally, the behaviour continues to deviate since now it is possible to access the root app route by including the root path in the request which was not possible with the CLI option. The OpenAPI schema is served with the root path prefixed so the Swagger UI can access it from outside the proxy, but now the UI does not show a "Failed to load API definition" Fetch error.

answer.body:
> Passing the `root_path` to FastAPI would be the equivalent of passing the `--root-path` command line option to Uvicorn or Hypercorn.

This statement in docs is not correct.
In fact, you should:
* use `--root-path` when you run app behind a proxy which **strips** part of the path
* use `root_path` parameter in the `FastAPI` constructor when you run app behind a proxy that **doesn't strip** part of the path

I opened PR to fix docs: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14238
